title: Confidential Information and Unauthorized Disclosure
definition: A secrecy violation occurs when a person discloses, shares, forwards, provides access to, or improperly handles confidential, restricted, proprietary, material non-public, or otherwise protected company information without appropriate authorization. The policy applies to the actual handling or disclosure of protected information, not merely to discussions about confidentiality or instructions to keep information confidential.
violations: Disclosing confidential or restricted company information to a person who is not authorized to receive it
Sharing confidential documents, files, information, business details, or protected data with an unauthorized external or internal recipient
Forwarding or providing access to protected company information without authorization
Improperly handling confidential information in a way that exposes it to unauthorized individuals
Requesting or encouraging another person to disclose protected company information without authorization
Sending protected information through an unauthorized communication channel when doing so exposes the information to an unauthorized person
Discussing protected information with a person who does not have a legitimate business need or authorization to receive it
exceptions: Legitimate instructions to keep information confidential
Instructions that prevent disclosure of information until an agreement, contract, or authorization is formally completed
Disclosure that is explicitly authorized by the appropriate company authority
Sharing information with a recipient who is explicitly authorized to receive it
Routine business communication that does not disclose protected or restricted information
Legitimate confidentiality agreements, non-disclosure agreements, or contract-related communications that do not themselves disclose protected information
examples: Sending a confidential company document to an unauthorized external recipient
Forwarding restricted business information to someone who is not authorized to receive it
Providing an unauthorized person with access to confidential company files
Sending protected company information to a personal account where the recipient is not authorized
Telling a recipient not to disclose an agreement until it has been formally signed is not itself an unauthorized disclosure
Discussing a confidentiality agreement without revealing protected information is not itself a secrecy violation

title: Improper Payments, Gifts, and Benefits
definition: A market bribery violation occurs when a person offers, promises, gives, requests, accepts, arranges, or suggests an improper payment, gift, benefit, favor, advantage, or personal benefit with the purpose or expectation of improperly influencing a business, commercial, regulatory, approval, procurement, or market-related decision. The benefit does not need to be money and does not need to have already been provided; a proposal or arrangement can itself constitute a violation when the intended influence is supported by the communication.
violations: Offering money or another improper benefit in exchange for favorable business treatment
Requesting or accepting an improper payment or benefit to influence a business decision
Offering a gift, favor, service, advantage, hospitality, or personal benefit with the intention of improperly influencing a decision
Agreeing to provide an improper benefit in return for preferential treatment
Using an intermediary or third party to provide an improper payment or benefit intended to influence a business decision
Discussing or arranging an improper payment or benefit for the purpose of obtaining an unfair business advantage
Suggesting that a gift, favor, gesture, payment, or personal benefit could help obtain approval, favorable treatment, access, or a business decision
Offering or suggesting a personal benefit to a decision maker in connection with obtaining a business approval or favorable outcome
exceptions: Legitimate business expenses that are permitted under applicable company policy
Ordinary business activities that do not involve an attempt to improperly influence a decision
Benefits that are explicitly permitted and appropriately authorized under company policy
Ordinary business hospitality that is reasonable, authorized, and not intended to influence a decision
examples: Offering money to a business partner in exchange for awarding a contract
Offering an inappropriate gift to influence a customer's purchasing decision
Requesting a personal payment in exchange for approving a business transaction
Arranging for another person to provide a benefit in exchange for preferential treatment
Suggesting that a small gesture for a decision maker could help obtain approval
Offering a favor to someone responsible for approving a business transaction

title: Artificial or Misleading Market Activity
definition: A market manipulation violation occurs when a person intentionally attempts to artificially influence the price, supply, demand, trading activity, market perception, or behavior of other market participants through deceptive, misleading, coordinated, or artificial actions. The violation may exist at the planning, proposal, coordination, instruction, or execution stage when the communication demonstrates an intention to create an artificial market effect.
violations: Intentionally creating artificial buying or selling activity to influence a market price
Coordinating transactions for the purpose of artificially increasing or decreasing a financial instrument's price
Creating false or misleading market activity to influence other market participants
Spreading false or misleading information with the intention of influencing trading activity or market prices
Using deceptive transactions or trading strategies to create a false impression of market demand or supply
Encouraging another person to participate in activity intended to artificially influence market conditions
Planning or coordinating activity around an announcement with the intention of producing a particular artificial market reaction
Coordinating otherwise legitimate-looking activity when the stated or implied purpose is to create an artificial market response
Discussing a planned action specifically because it is expected to make the market react in a desired way
exceptions: Legitimate market analysis that does not involve deceptive or artificial activity
Ordinary trading or investment decisions made for legitimate business or investment purposes
Accurate communication of publicly available market information without an intention to mislead
Legitimate discussion of market conditions without instructions to manipulate market activity
Legitimate planning of business activity where the purpose is not to create an artificial market effect
examples: Coordinating transactions specifically to artificially increase the price of a security
Creating misleading trading activity to make market demand appear higher than it actually is
Sharing intentionally false information to influence another person's trading decision
Planning transactions specifically to create an artificial market price
Coordinating activity around an announcement because the participants expect the market to react in a desired way
Planning activity specifically to cause or control an expected market reaction

title: Employee Ethical Conduct and Appropriate Workplace Communication
definition: An employee ethics violation occurs when an employee uses official company communication or workplace interactions for inappropriate, unprofessional, personal, social, dishonest, deceptive, or otherwise unacceptable conduct that conflicts with expected workplace behavior. The policy requires contextual interpretation: personal or social content is not automatically a violation, and legitimate business activities involving meals, drinks, entertainment, hospitality, events, or social interaction are not violations when they are authorized and relevant to legitimate company activity.
violations: Using official company email or communication channels for inappropriate personal or social discussion unrelated to legitimate business activity
Discussing alcohol, drinks, drinking, partying, or similar personal activities in an official business communication when the discussion is unrelated to legitimate business activity
Discussing personal entertainment, parties, social gatherings, or recreational activities in an official business communication when the discussion is inappropriate or unrelated to business
Sending inappropriate personal messages through official company communication channels
Using company communication channels for inappropriate personal arrangements or requests
Engaging in inappropriate, unprofessional, disrespectful, or improper communication with employees or business contacts
Making inappropriate personal requests, suggestions, or arrangements through official company communication
Using workplace relationships or company communication channels to facilitate inappropriate personal activities
Using company resources or official communication channels for unauthorized personal purposes
Knowingly providing false or misleading information for an improper purpose
Using an employee's position, authority, access, or influence for an improper personal benefit
Engaging in dishonest or deceptive conduct related to company business
Intentionally changing, falsifying, concealing, or misrepresenting business information or figures for an improper purpose
Changing figures, records, reports, or business information to make results appear more favorable when the change is misleading or dishonest
Intentionally concealing relevant information to obtain an improper benefit
Engaging in an undisclosed or improperly managed conflict of interest
Attempting to conceal inappropriate or improper employee conduct
exceptions: Legitimate business communication
Legitimate company-sponsored social activities
Authorized business entertainment or hospitality
Business-related discussion of meals, drinks, entertainment, or events when relevant to legitimate company activity
Professional communication that is appropriate for the business context
Clearly personal communication that is not sent through an official company communication channel
Good-faith business decisions
Ordinary mistakes that do not involve improper conduct
Communication that is directly relevant to an authorized company event or activity
Accurate correction of figures or information for a legitimate business purpose
Good-faith preparation or formatting of a report that does not misrepresent the underlying information
examples: Using an official company email to discuss personal drinking or drinks unrelated to business
Discussing plans for partying or personal entertainment through an official business email without a legitimate business purpose
Using a company email to arrange an inappropriate personal social activity
Sending inappropriate personal messages through an official company communication channel
Using company communication to arrange a personal activity unrelated to work
Discussing drinks as part of an authorized company event is not automatically a violation
Discussing a business dinner or authorized company entertainment is not automatically a violation
A legitimate business discussion involving hospitality is not an ethics violation

A message such as 'so who are the drinks on until I do ???' in an official business email should be evaluated as Employee ethics because it contains inappropriate personal/social content in an official business communication
Changing figures before sharing a report so that the results appear more favorable may constitute dishonest or misleading conduct
Knowingly altering business figures to create a misleading impression of performance is an Employee ethics violation

title: Complaint Handling and Reporting
definition: A complaints-related violation occurs when a legitimate complaint, concern, allegation, or report involving employee conduct, business practices, or company processes is improperly ignored, suppressed, mishandled, discouraged, concealed, or intentionally prevented from reaching the appropriate reporting, investigation, compliance, or review process.
violations: Intentionally preventing a legitimate complaint from being reported through the appropriate process
Ignoring a complaint that requires investigation or appropriate handling
Suppressing or concealing a legitimate complaint or concern
Improperly handling a formal complaint in a way that prevents appropriate review
Discouraging a person from reporting a legitimate concern through an approved reporting process
Retaliating against or improperly treating a person because they raised a legitimate complaint
Instructing or encouraging someone not to report a legitimate complaint or concern
Attempting to prevent a complaint from reaching compliance, HR, legal, management, or another appropriate reporting function
Deliberately delaying or obstructing a complaint investigation for an improper purpose
exceptions: A person simply reporting a legitimate concern or complaint
Routine communication about a complaint that does not suppress, ignore, or improperly handle the complaint
Resolving a complaint through an authorized company process
Requesting additional information needed to properly investigate a complaint
Directing a complaint to the correct authorized reporting or investigation channel
examples: Telling an employee not to report a legitimate workplace concern
Ignoring a formal complaint that requires investigation
Attempting to prevent a complaint from reaching the appropriate compliance team
Suppressing a legitimate complaint to avoid an investigation
Encouraging someone to keep a legitimate complaint informal so that it is not reported

title: Unauthorized Communication Channels
definition: A change in communication violation occurs when business-related communication is moved, continued, redirected, or intentionally invited from an approved company communication channel to a personal or external communication channel that is not approved for company business. The context of the surrounding communication must establish that the external channel is intended for company business rather than clearly personal communication.
violations: Moving a business discussion from an approved company channel to a personal or external communication channel
Asking another person to continue business-related communication through a personal or external messaging service
Using a personal or external communication service to continue discussions concerning company business, agreements, transactions, or other work-related matters
Redirecting business communication to an external channel specifically to avoid or bypass an approved company communication system
Continuing a business discussion through an external communication method when the communication concerns company work or a business agreement
Inviting a business contact to communicate about work through a personal messaging application
Providing a personal phone number, personal email address, messaging account, or external messaging account for the purpose of continuing company business outside an approved channel
Suggesting that business communication continue through WhatsApp, personal messaging, personal email, or another external service when the surrounding context is company business
exceptions: The external communication channel is explicitly approved for the relevant business activity
The communication is clearly personal and unrelated to company business
The external channel is being used for a legitimate purpose specifically authorized by the company
An approved business process explicitly requires the use of the external channel
examples: Asking a business contact to continue a company discussion through a personal messaging service
Moving a discussion about a business agreement to an external messaging application
Asking someone to continue company-related communication through a personal account
Inviting a business contact to continue work-related communication outside the approved company communication system
Discussing a business agreement and then saying 'Feel free to ding me on WhatsApp anytime'
Providing a personal messaging account specifically so a business discussion can continue outside the approved company channel
